items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: I was getting into that and that's where I met Red Norvo... I got to play in it... I did that in Red Norvo's band, still playing trumpet then.

ctx.x: Around that time I guess you were with Charlie Barnett; right?

I was getting into that and that's where I met Red Norvo. But before that--remember we were talking about Cozy Cole, with the kids band I was in; at the same time I was in Columbia Blue Lions, ran them both--I didn't run Columbia but the other one I was involved in. We got a job at the--this was the Empire Ballroom, and Benny Carter and the other band--we were the relief band--

items.title: 56799_Red Norvo oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Sauter was writing pretty well, and he was doing some great arrangements for Mildred, also some good things for the band.

ctx.x: -- all her things she had complete control of anything that she did. Yet, it used to amaze me ah -- how easygoing she would go about things. She'd come into a song, she'd say, 'Dave, play it over on the piano.' And she'd put it up and he'd play it over a couple of times, she'd kind of listen to it, listen to it, and she'd do it. It used to amaze me. Even later, when we were working together, we'd have tunes to record, and Eddie Sauter would be writing them, and she'd be getting for the record date, she'd say,…
words up, gible) go through it once, she's ready to record.

items.title: 56799_Red Norvo oral history interview
items.q: Brass was -- let's see, Stewie Fletcher, P Hyland Eddie Sauter and Bill Highland.
